stories.title: Russia-China trade rises 22% in 1H 2026, exceeds $135 bln
stories.summary: Denis Manturov also added that during meetings held in Beijing in May and most recently in Bishkek, the leaders of Russia and China praised the development of trade and economic cooperation, which is one of the key pillars of bilateral relations
article_sentences: Trade between Russia and China increased by 22% in the first half of 2026, exceeding $135 bln, Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov said at a meeting of the Russian-Chinese Intergovernmental Commission on Investment Cooperation on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum (EEF).
According to him, the current pace is steadily bringing the two countries closer to their $300 bln target.
Manturov also noted that bilateral trade returned to growth this year.
"In the first half of the year, bilateral trade increased by 22% and exceeded $135 bln," he said.

Manturov also added that during meetings held in Beijing in May and most recently in Bishkek, the leaders of Russia and China praised the development of trade and economic cooperation, which is one of the key pillars of bilateral relations.

stories.headline: Beijing sends coastguard to conduct ‘law enforcement’ patrol near Taiwan

opening: Beijing said it conducted a routine patrol in waters east of Taiwan on Thursday, the latest in weeks of ramped-up activity by coastguard and other vessels that has alarmed the island.
China Coast Guard spokesman Jiang Lue said a formation led by the Putuoshan vessel carried out a “law enforcement” patrol “in accordance with the law”.
body: He said the formation had strengthened control over the waters since last month, safeguarding the rights and interests of Chinese citizens.

stories.title: Rosatom signs contract to build Balkhash NPP in Kazakhstan at EEF
stories.summary: Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev said that "the document signed today marks a new stage in cooperation with Kazakhstan"
article_sentences: Russia's Rosatom State Nuclear Energy Corporation and Kazakhstan Nuclear Power Plants signed a contract at the Eastern Economic Forum (EEF) to build the two-unit Balkhash Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) with a total generating capacity of 2,400 MW.
"The document signed today marks a new stage in our cooperation with Kazakhstan.
In the near future, Rosatom will carry out design work and establish an international consortium of equipment suppliers.
At every stage of the project, we will remain firmly focused on our main objective: to build and commission power units that meet the strictest international safety and efficiency requirements.

We are confident that Russian nuclear technologies will provide a reliable foundation for the Republic of Kazakhstan's energy independence and sustainable development," Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev said.
On June 14, 2025, Rosatom was selected to lead the international consortium that will build Kazakhstan's first high-capacity nuclear power plant.
In June 2025, at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum, Rosatom and Kazakhstan's Atomic Energy Agency approved an indicative roadmap for the nuclear power plant construction project.
